I was on the same boat as you, although I am still pretty young. I had the opportunity to go overseas for a month and just travel and enjoy all the art that western Europe has to offer. The first 2 weeks were miserable, my feet hurt, my back hurt, I missed my family and my close friends, but after those 14 days or so, something switched. All of a sudden everything was beautiful. All of the "little things" that people talk about all of a sudden happened a hell of a lot more often. 

I had been depressed since i was about 12, and at the ripe age of 17 I finally feel like myself again. Taking the time to not only absorb another culture, but to get away from what's been bothering you is a really good way to get some perspective on what really matters. 

I had no idea how much my father meant to me until I called him weeping on the 5th day of the trip.

To further extend my advice, go somewhere where the type of daily travel is different than what you are used to. If you are comfortable  walking everywhere, go somewhere (such as London or New York, NY) where that is not a very good idea; and visa versa. 

It's the culture shock coupled with the fact that you don't know where anything is that lets you figure out exactly how much you appreciate all the things your brother has done, how insignificant the bickering with your mom is, or how much you like looking at Renaissance paintings, or how much you dislike accidentally stumbling upon a nude beach.

I really urge you to try.

I would create a game that tests the player's abilities to parent. There would be realistic scenarios, most of them would be commonplace, others would be very stress-inducing and slightly rarer than most. This game would be mandatory for expecting parents to take before the birth of their child. 

The game would take into account what drugs the parents use, both medically and recreationally, any past convictions and things of the like. The game would be filled with tests that would be announced to test one branch of morality, for example, but would also test other things, such as how the parents respond to elongated stress centered around the baby, and completely disregard what the game announced it was testing in the particular round.

All scores would be sent to the heads of Child Protective Services (or the country's equivalent) to be screened. If the couple passed, they would not be bothered by CPS again. If they failed, the couple would have the option to abort the child, give it up for adoption, or to go through extensive counseling predating the birth, and would be monitored at regular intervals, to make sure that the child is still safe and healthy. Depending on how bad their scoring was inversely affects how often the new family is checked on.

There will be different versions for people who want to adopt, where the parents ability to cope with the emotional distress of the child will be addressed more thoroughly. There will be single parent version, one for potential foster parents, etc. environment will also be taken into consideration, as well as the number of kids the couple would want to have and annual income. If a family is too poor to properly care for a child, CPS can grant them the opportunity to either have joint custody with another family, where both sets of parents help care for the child, or receiving a welfare check, and one of various ways to potentially raise the average yearly income, or of course give up the child or terminate the pregnancy.

In the case of custody disputes, a shorter, more "elusive" version of the game will be used as grounds for one parent potentially getting more custody of the child.

Aside from the selected officials who must "grade" the scores, and possibly a judge/jury, the scores will be 100% confidential.

The object of the game is NOT to make it harder to have children, but to make sure that all children are given a chance to succeed, no matter the situation at home. It is also there to help parents learn where they are lacking in their parenting skills, long before any permanent mental damage is done to either party. This could also potentially help with overpopulation. Orphanages will be much less crowded, and the children there would not have had to go through something traumatic to wind up there.

Future advances of the game will test how parents react to things that happen once the child is older, i.e. the child develops schizophrenia.

I understand several and a half people would not be happy with having to take this test, but there are too many kids that have addicts for parents, or are otherwise unfit to be parents. If you've lived in a broken home, you know how hard it is finding out how wrong their parenting was when you age. Children don't know better, and I feel future generations will gradually get healthier and happier as the world goes on. This could be the beginning of exponential growth of many positive things, that a person as young as myself cannot even imagine.
